identity.author: John Davenant
identity.work: Two Dissertations (De praedestinatione through Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol partial)
identity.edition: Dissertationes duae (Cambridge: Roger Daniel, 1650). Partial through Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol (common providence). Angel gifts analogy / further Arg. 10 remain.

scope.locus: De praedestinatione Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol close + Arg. 10 + Sol start.
scope.next_locus: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont. (angel gifts not subordinated to ruin; Thomas on predestination vs providence).

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol close: creating Judas the reprobate is not creating him that he may be damned — as feeding a thief sentenced to die is not feeding him that he may die
english: God is rightly said to act for some intended end when he gives things a nature ordered to that end. But in creating Judas God did not give him a nature ordained to damnation. So it is false to hold that the creation of Judas the reprobate has this intention — that it be a medium advanced toward damnation. It is one thing to create a man reprobate and to be damned for his demerits; another to create him that he may be damned — as it is one thing to feed, clothe, and comfort a thief sentenced to die, another to do those things that he may die.
sections.latin: Deum recte dici agere propter intentum aliquem finem, cum rebus talem dat naturam ut sint propter talem finem: Deus autem creando Judam non dedit illi naturam ad damnationem ordinatam: Falso igitur statuitur creatio Judae reprobati habere hanc intentionem, ut medium sit quod ad damnationem provehatur. Aliud enim est creare hominem reprobatum et ob demerita sua damnandum, aliud creare ut damnetur; sicut aliud est alere, vestire, solari latronem damnandum, aliud haec facere ut damnetur.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol close: God creates in time those not predestined to beatitude — creation's proper end is communication of good, not damnation as intended scope
english: So God creates in time those he from eternity did not predestine to beatitude — whom he foresaw would by their own fault rush to voluntary ruin, whom he decreed to permit to fall into this everlasting misery. Yet men's creation (which in the order of decreeing preceded all that) had its own proper end: God's glory in the diffusion and communication of good — not their damnation, which is to be held an event following the creation of the reprobate, not a scope intended by God as creator.
sections.latin: Creat ergo Deus in tempore, quos ab aeterno minime praedestinavit ad beatitudinem, quos praevidit sua culpa ad interitum ruituros voluntarium, quos decrevit permittere ut inciderent in hanc miseriam sempiternam: sed interim creatio hominum (quae ordine decernendi haec omnia praecessit) habuit proprium suum finem, Dei gloriam in diffusione ac communicatione boni, non damnationem eorundem, quae habenda est eventus consequens creationem reprobatorum, non scopus intentus a Deo creante.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol close: Scripture sounding as if God created some unto contumely is to be read permissively — vessels of contumely by not adding special grace
english: And last: wherever Scripture seems to speak as though God had fashioned some for disgrace and ruin, I judge those places to be taken permissively. Day by day he brings into being those whom, under the decree of non-election or of reprobation, he suffers to turn into vessels of contumely — withholding the special grace that would have made them vessels of honor.
sections.latin: Denique, si quae loca Scripturae in hunc sensum sonare videantur, quasi Deus creasset aliquos in contumeliam et perditionem, sunt, meo quidem judicio, interpretanda permissive. Creat enim indies, quos secundum decretum non-electionis seu reprobationis permittit fieri vasa contumeliae, non apponendo illam specialem gratiam quae faceret eos vasa honoris.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 10: if election and reprobation hang on mere liberty of will, Gospel preaching to the reprobate becomes from God's precise intention a ministry of condemnation
english: If we set election and reprobation as hanging on mere liberty of divine will — not on the differing acts of elect and reprobate themselves (these' penitence, those' impenitence; these' persevering faith, those' final unbelief) — then Gospel preaching toward the reprobate, from God's nearest precise intention, will be a ministry of condemnation, and will not be set before them from God's first intention to work their salvation, but as a medium subordinated to damnation in executing the reprobation decree. That fights the Gospel ministry head-on, since from God's first intention it is a ministry of life.
sections.latin: Si ponamus electionem et reprobationem ex mera libertate Divinae voluntatis pendentem, et non ex discriminatis actibus ipsorum electorum et reprobatorum (puta horum poenitentia, illorum impoenitentia, horum fide perseverante, illorum finali infidelitate): tum Evangelii praedicatio quoad reprobatos ex proxima et precisa Dei intentione erit ministerium condemnationis, et non proponetur ipsis ex prima Dei intentione ad salutem ipsorum operandam, sed ut medium exsequendo decreto reprobationis damnationi subordinatum. At hoc directe cum ministerio Evangelii pugnat, utpote quod ex prima Dei intentione est ministerium vitae.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol: Major's consequence invalid — not everything later done about the non-elect flows from absolute reprobation; Vasquez: some effects are of common providence
english: We answer that the Major's consequence is invalid. The adversaries err in this: having posited absolute reprobation, they take it as following that whatever is later done about these non-elect or reprobate flows from that decree. Vasquez rightly notes the contrary: neither in the predestined nor in the reprobate is every effect of God's providence an effect of predestination or reprobation — some is an effect of common providence (In 1 q.23 a.4 c.4 disp. 93).
sections.latin: Consequentiam Majoris invalidam esse respondemus; atque in hoc falli adversarios affirmamus, quod posito absolutae reprobationis decreto quasi consequens assumunt, ex hoc decreto manare quicquid postea circa hosce non-electos sive reprobatos peragitur. At e contra recte observavit Vasques, Nec in praedestinato nec in reprobato omnem effectum providentiae Dei esse praedestinationis aut reprobationis, sed aliquem esse effectum communis providentiae, In 1. quaest. 23. artic. 4. cap. 4. disp. 93.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol: God knows Gospel benefits will harm reprobates and decreed not to add softening grace — yet preaching is not from primary intention a medium of damnation
english: We grant God knows Gospel preaching and his other benefits will be harmful to these reprobates. We grant further that no reprobate's will is so wild and intractable that God cannot soften it to faith and penitence — that is, to the effect of obeying. We grant finally that God has decreed with himself not to apply to these reprobates that special efficacious grace by which they would be softened. All that granted, we still deny that Gospel preaching, or that gift of scantier commoner grace, is proposed from a primary nearest intention of damning, or ought to be judged media subordinated to damnation. From foresight, or God's permission, or a following event, we may not infer that God's primary intention, and the subordination of media, aimed at producing that event.
sections.latin: Concedimus quidem, Deum scire Evangelii praedicationem, aliaque omnia sua beneficia hisce reprobatis fore noxia; concedimus insuper, nullius reprobati voluntatem tam feram tamque intratabilem esse, quin possit Deus illam ad fidem et poenitentiam (hoc est, ad obediendi effectum) emollire; concedimus denique, Deum decrevisse apud se hisce reprobatis non apponere illam gratiam specialem et efficacem, qua emollirentur: Sed hisce omnibus positis negamus, aut Evangelii praedicationem, aut illam parcitoris et communioris gratiae donationem ex primaria et proxima intentione damnandi proponi, aut tanquam media damnationi subordinata judicari oportere. Non enim debemus ex praevisione, aut permissione Dei, aut ex eventu subsequente inferre primariam Dei intentionem, et mediorum subordinationem ad talem eventum producendum spectasse.
